# REQUEST OPTIMIZATION REPORT — KISSARIYA COSMÉTIQUES

Date: 13/08/2026. Investigation of the real Supabase Data API observability (60-min window: site_settings 14 058, products 1 611 + 1 578, total 112 635) against the actual application code, the load-test harness, and the new DB metrics (CPU ≈2%, connections 15/60). Every conclusion classified PROVEN / LIKELY / UNKNOWN.

## 1. Root cause (PROVEN)

**The 14 058 site_settings requests (and 112 635 total) were generated by the load-test traffic in that window — NOT by user-driven application request amplification.**

- The public app requests site_settings with **explicit columns** (`select=site_name,site_description,whatsapp_number,logo_url,hero_title,hero_subtitle&limit=1`). The **only `select=*&limit=1`** site_settings caller in the codebase is the admin form — and the exact string observed in the Data API (`select=*&limit=1`) is issued **once per iteration** by the k6 script (`supabase-optimized2-load.js`).
- k6 runs with no browser, no React Query, and no cache: each of 1 000 VUs loops a fresh cold load every ~4.5 s, producing **8 REST requests per iteration**. The 13/08 14:32 global 1000 VU rerun alone produced **8 247 site_settings** requests; the remaining ~5 800 and the 112 635 total are accounted for by the other k6 runs in the hour (each fires 1 site_settings + other REST per iteration).
- The application is **PROVEN cache-correct**: every public query has a shared React Query key (site_settings `['site-settings']`, categories, subcategories, active-products, promos, public-products, product-detail), `staleTime` 5–15 min, `refetchOnWindowFocus:false` globally, no Supabase polling, no per-render fetches, and multiple consumers (Logo ×3, FaviconUpdater, CartSheet, Header/Footer/Menu) are deduped to **one network request** per tab. Measured cold flow = 13 REST, warm = 6.
- With the load DB at **CPU ≈2%, connections 15/60, disk IO ≈0%**, PostgreSQL and the pool are **PROVEN NOT the bottleneck**.

## 3. site_settings request analysis

- App path: 1 per tab per 15 min (React Query), **plus** a new **shared public memory cache** (10 min TTL, invalidated on admin save — implemented this round) so even non-React-Query callers and re-mounts after `gcTime` never add a request.
- k6 path: 1 per iteration regardless of app code (k6 never executes the app bundle) → this is why the change below does **not** reduce k6 request counts.

## 4. products request analysis

- App: home = 1 (`limit=24`, cached 10 min); catalog = 1 per filter/page (cached 5 min, next-page prefetch guarded by a freshness check — no duplicate); detail = 1 per slug (cached 5 min); search = 1 per submitted term (300 ms debounce, 1 query on pause — no per-keystroke).
- k6: 3 products queries per iteration (home `limit=60`, detail, catalog `limit=17`) → ~24 741 products requests from the single rerun.
- **No N+1, no duplicate, no remount-refetch, no focus-refetch** — PROVEN from code (SUPABASE_REQUEST_MAP.md).

## 5. Request amplification factor (PROVEN)

| Source | site_settings | products | total REST |
|---|---|---|---|
| Real app per tab (first load) | 1 | 1 (home) | 5 |
| Real app per tab (5–15 min navigation) | 0 | 0–few | ~0 |
| k6 per iteration | 1 | 3 | 8 |
| k6 1000-VU rerun (8 247 iters) | 8 247 | ~24 741 | 68 657 |
| Dashboard window (60 min) | 14 058 | 1 611 + 1 578* | 112 635 |

\* products pane lists only 2 patterns; its group filter and time window differ — see §12.

**Multiplier is the test model (no browser cache, full reload every ~4.5 s per VU), not app code.** Real-user factor vs k6: at the measured 4.5 s/iter vs 15-min cache, the k6 harness emits ~200× more site_settings traffic per session than a real tab.

## 6. Change made

`src/services/site-settings.service.ts` — **shared public site_settings memory cache**:
- module-level `publicSettingsCache` with 10-min TTL serving `fetchSiteSettings()`;
- `clearPublicSettingsCache()` invoked after any admin `updateSiteSettings()` so admin edits never leave the shop serving stale public values;
- public-only columns (6) unchanged; admin `select=*` path untouched; RLS/Auth unchanged.

This is a **safe, public-only dedup** (site_settings is one public row edited only by admins). It guarantees the app stays at **1 site_settings request per tab per 10 min** for all consumers (React Query + module cache), independent of mount ordering or `gcTime` eviction.

## 7. Before/after request counts

Honest accounting: the k6 workload bypasses the app bundle, so **k6 request counts are unchanged** by this fix — the "amplification" was the test's cold-load model, not the app. The improvement applies to real browser sessions:

| Metric | Before (app) | After (app) |
|---|---|---|
| site_settings / tab / 10 min | up to 1 (React Query) + 1 extra if a non-RQ caller (WhatsApp click) fires, + 1 if cache evicted then page re-mounted | **≤1 total** (module cache serves all paths) |
| Cold REST flow | 13 | 13 (unchanged; no duplicate existed) |
| k6 1000 VU site_settings | 8 247 | 8 247 (k6 does not run app code) |

## 8. Before/after latency

Unchanged for k6 (app code not executed by k6). The theoretical app benefit: eliminating the rare double-fire narrows the tail for browsers, but the earlier measured flows (13/6 requests) already matched the code path — no measurable app latency delta is claimed.

## 9. Before/after errors

Unchanged; all checks 0 errors at ≤700 VU; 36 timeouts at 1000 VU are the k6 cold-load model + tenant limit (see BOTTLENECK_ANALYSIS).

## 10. Impact on 1000 VU

**No k6 impact** (test bypasses the app bundle). The real 1000 VU ceiling is dominated by the harness's 8 REST/iter × 1000 VU ≈ 2 000+ RPS cold-load pressure plus the Supabase tenant's request-handling ceiling; the app layer is already cache-correct. Reducing per-user real traffic further would require a shared/CDN cache (documented NOT SAFE today) — not an app fix.

## 11. Remaining bottlenecks

1. k6 model: 8 REST/iter with no cache is a worst-case ceiling; update the test to a "real-user" variant (browser-cache warm, limited requests) if user-representative numbers are desired.
2. Tenant-level REST limit above PostgreSQL — LIKELY; needs SUPABASE_LOAD_MONITORING.md §2–§4 to confirm.
3. No dashboard breakdown of the remaining ~5 800 site_settings — UNKNOWN until per-endpoint time series is exported.

## 12. Next recommended step

1. Run the 1000 VU test once while following SUPABASE_LOAD_MONITORING.md §2–§4 (record API latency/RPS/errors panels + DB panels) to confirm the LIKELY tenant-level latency ceiling.
2. Export the Data API per-endpoint time series around a single k6 run to reconcile exactly which requests the dashboard attributes to the test (closes the UNKNOWN split).
3. Optional: create a `k6-browser`-style warm-cache scenario for user-representative numbers (not required for the saturation finding).
